solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drive for soldiers with nameless drug

parts.note: being for something is being pro it
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: nameless says the abbreviation for name, a single N, is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: with means and, joining things together
E is slang shorthand for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer's errand: driving off to supply troops with an unbranded narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' acts on 'with' (AND), not on the drug: AND loses its N to give AD, and the drug is just E.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a place or outing for leisurely walking or driving, so a drive along the front fits.

clue.text: Westminster Abbey is a royal one — strange!

definitions.text: Westminster Abbey is a royal one
definitions.meaning: a royal ... is a church answerable to the monarch rather than a bishop, as Westminster Abbey is

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at the abbey's royal status.
explanation.definitionFit: A church outside its bishop's jurisdiction is a royal peculiar; as an adjective the word means odd.

clue.text: In highly decorated style or neatly arranged

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of neatly are put in a new order after the or

explanation.surface: A choice between fussy decoration and tidy arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reorders NEATLY into NATELY; OR stays in front as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes something done with elaborate ornament.

clue.text: The greatest challenges for statesmen?

parts.note: Harold Macmillan, asked what most threw governments off course, is said to have replied with a famous two-word quip

explanation.surface: A question about what most tests political leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: British prime minister Harold Macmillan supposedly answered 'Events, dear boy, events' when asked what a statesman most feared.
explanation.definitionFit: Unforeseen happenings are what Macmillan named as the hardest thing for a leader to handle.

clue.text: Desserts are cooked faster

indicators.note: cooked suggests the word faster has been reworked into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Puddings are prepared more quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are cooked' rearranges FASTER. Afters is British slang for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage calls the sweet course that follows the main meal by this name.

clue.text: It's possible to avoid priest losing head on board

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the priest's name goes

parts.note: Levi founded the priestly tribe of Israel, the Levites
a table is a board, as in a board laid for a meal

explanation.surface: A priest losing his head aboard ship could have been avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts LEVI to EVI; 'on' just joins it to TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evitable is the rare opposite of inevitable: avoidable, capable of being escaped.

clue.text: Work on stage right several years

parts.note: OP, opposite prompt, is the theatre term for stage right
an era is a span of many years

explanation.surface: An actor's job taking place on the right of the stage for years on end.
explanation.walkthrough: OP stands for 'opposite prompt', the side of a stage across from the prompter, which is stage right.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for work, and its plural names a musical stage composition.

clue.text: One appearing at 13 across could be roasting

indicators.note: could be says the letters of roasting may turn into another word

explanation.surface: A performer at the hall might be getting very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ROASTING. The Royal Albert Hall houses a famous large pipe organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Albert Hall's great organ means a keyboard player of that instrument often performs there.

clue.text: Queen held by senseless revolutionary in 6 across

indicators.note: held by says the queen's letter sits inside the other piece
revolutionary says the word for senseless is turned round

parts.note: inane means senseless or silly
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A monarch taken prisoner by a mindless rebel in an opera plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns INANE into ENANI, and 'held by' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernani is Verdi's 1844 opera based on a Victor Hugo play.

clue.text: American husband embraces returning slave once more

indicators.note: embraces says the first pair of letters wraps around the rest
returning says the word for a slave is read backwards

parts.note: a serf is a bonded labourer, a kind of slave

explanation.surface: A US husband hugs a slave who has come back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the slave word and 'embraces' puts the result between the American and husband letters; the surface's husband is just an H.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something afresh means starting it again from the beginning.

clue.text: This pitch has now been standardised

definitions.text: This pitch has now been standardised

parts.words: This pitch has now been standardised
parts.note: ... pitch is the tuning standard, with the A above middle C fixed at 440 hertz

explanation.surface: A remark that some field or level has at last been made uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to the phrase 'concert pitch', the agreed tuning reference for orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard tuning musicians use is named after the musical performance at which it is used.

clue.text: Provide premature death of former Secretary-General almost in freedom from pain

indicators.note: in says that the shortened name goes inside the word for freedom from pain

parts.note: ease is relief from pain or discomfort

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of that name is dropped

parts.note: U Thant was Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1961 to 1971

explanation.surface: A grim note on whether a retired UN chief, nearly free of pain, should be helped to die early.
explanation.walkthrough: U Thant, the Burmese diplomat who led the UN in the 1960s, loses his last letter ('almost'), and 'in' sets him inside the word for relief.
explanation.definitionFit: To euthanase is to bring about a merciful early death, the verb behind euthanasia.

clue.text: Obstructions returning priest puts to some purpose

indicators.note: returning says the priest's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel
to use something is to put it to a purpose

explanation.surface: A cleric coming back and making use of barriers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ELI into ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileus is a medical blockage of the intestine, so the plural names several such obstructions.

clue.text: This 18 down regularly appears at 13 across

definitions.text: This 18 down regularly appears at 13 across

parts.words: This 18 down regularly appears at 13 across
parts.note: the Royal ... Legion, the veterans' charity, holds its annual Festival of Remembrance at the London concert hall

explanation.surface: A note that a certain legion turns up at a certain venue every year.
explanation.walkthrough: With 18 down it makes the British Legion, which runs the Festival of Remembrance in the Royal Albert Hall each November.
explanation.definitionFit: The veterans' charity that stages its remembrance festival at the hall is the British Legion.

clue.text: See 12a

parts.note: the clue at 12 across says the British Legion regularly appears at this place, so that clue serves as the definition here: the Kensington concert venue hosting the Festival of Remembrance

explanation.walkthrough: The light has no clue of its own: 12 across, which with 18 down is the British Legion, says where that charity holds its annual Festival of Remembrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Legion's Festival of Remembrance has been staged each November at this domed Kensington concert hall.

clue.text: Game's over among the French

indicators.note: among says the word for over sits inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
across means over, as in going over to the other side

explanation.surface: The match is finished as far as the French are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game's' is 'Game is'; the 's is a link. 'over' is not 'finished' but across, and 'among' puts it inside the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with long-handled netted sticks.

clue.text: Went first round loft and fretted

indicators.note: round says the leading word goes around the roof-space word

parts.note: led means went first, as at the front of a line
an attic is a loft under the roof

explanation.surface: Someone went ahead around the attic and worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fretted' is not 'worried' here: fretwork is an interlaced decorative pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretted work is carved in an interlacing pattern, which is a crisscross trellis design.

clue.text: Disapproval of result when lights are lowered …

definitions.meaning: taking this of something means disapproving of it
literally, a dimmed outlook when the lamps are turned down

explanation.surface: Turning the lights down leaves people unimpressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for frowning on something, read literally, is what you see in low light.

clue.text: Smokers use them in boats

definitions.meaning: small devices that produce a flame for cigarettes
flat-bottomed barges used to ferry goods to and from ships

explanation.surface: People who smoke carry these on board.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cigarette igniter and an unloading barge.

clue.text: Dead skin is not producing delayed stroke

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died

indicators.note: not tells us the word is is to be left out of the skin word

parts.note: cutis is the anatomical word for skin

explanation.surface: A medical finding: the dead skin is failing to produce anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not' removes IS from CUTIS to leave CUT. A late cut is a cricket shot played late, steering the ball behind the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the late cut is a shot played with the stroke left till the last moment.

clue.text: Many on one forward

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
I is the Roman numeral one
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A crowd aboard, one moving ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a vast host, so the word means a great many.

clue.text: Where 10 and 60% of 24 make game

parts.note: ten is the number written in words
the answer at 24 across has five letters, and sixty per cent of them is its first three

explanation.surface: A riddle about where certain numbers combine into a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' means 24 across, the goblin NISSE, though the other cross-references in this puzzle say across or down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played across a net.

clue.text: Where Rhone joins Rhine perhaps

parts.note: Rhone and Rhine are wine regions, and their wines meet side by side when judged at a sampling session

explanation.surface: A geography question about where two great European rivers meet.
explanation.walkthrough: The rivers never actually meet; here they are wines, Rhone and Rhine (hock), brought together on the same table.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine sampling event is where bottles from different regions are set side by side.

clue.text: Rocks very large chests

parts.note: tors are rocky hilltops, as on Dartmoor
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: Boulders form really big boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chests' is the body's trunk, not a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is the human trunk, the part of the body that holds the chest.

clue.text: Magnificent bird leaves American football match

indicators.note: leaves says the bird departs from the football match word

parts.note: the Super Bowl is the championship game of American football
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A splendid bird walks out of an NFL game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes OWL from SUPERBOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is a synonym of splendid or excellent.

clue.text: Light 6 across has more than one try with broken old rein

definitions.text: Light 6 across has more than one

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: broken says the letters of old and rein are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bright opera features several attempts with a snapped old harness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light 6 across' is a light opera, The Gondoliers by Gilbert and Sullivan, whose title has more than one of the answer. 'broken' scrambles OLD REIN into NDOLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gondoliers is the Savoy opera named after several Venetian boatmen of this kind.

clue.text: Reptiles lacking power could become unproductive

indicators.note: could become says the remaining letters change into a new arrangement
lacking says the power letter is taken away from the reptiles word

explanation.surface: A worry that reptiles short of energy may fail to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes P from REPTILES, and 'could become' rearranges the remaining RETILES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means barren, unable to produce offspring or results.

clue.text: Most of hut used by friendly goblin

indicators.note: most of says the last letter of the hut word is dropped

parts.note: a Nissen hut is a corrugated-iron shelter with a half-cylinder roof

explanation.surface: A kindly goblin who has taken over most of a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nissen hut is the curved corrugated-iron shelter used widely in Britain in both world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scandinavian folklore a nisse is a benevolent household sprite.

clue.text: Instruction to maid in drought areas?

definitions.meaning: an order to a housemaid to wipe the dishes clean
regions of parched, wind-eroded land such as the 1930s American prairies

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a command it tells a servant to clean the bowls; as a noun it names arid, blown-away farmland.
